 # Research status
 
+## All-field ranks of single-top-polynomial biforms
+
+The [top-coefficient biform theorem](research/ai/2026-10-23-top-coefficient-biforms/proof.md) computes the literal cyclic-source matrix R_(a,b) for every f(x,z)=c_0+...+c_(e-1)*z^(e-1)+w(x)*z^e with 1<=e<b, nonzero constant c_0, constant lower coefficients, and nonzero polynomial w of x-degree d<a. Over every field, its exact rank is ab + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b,d*floor((a+j)/e)). The leading polynomial-kernel vectors form a triangular residue basis, giving a complete all-field proof. The new controls pass 3,372 full-matrix modular comparisons and 24 independent-implementation rational matrix ranks. Claim AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 is proof-written-unreviewed. It does not classify arbitrary quadratic-in-z coefficients, build a three-leg tensor target, or improve omega below 9/4. The separate [continuation](research/ai/2026-10-23-top-coefficient-biforms/CONTINUATION.md) records exact scope and provenance.

+# Exact ranks for biforms with one polynomial top coefficient
+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed AI-assisted research. Claim AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 is proof-written-unreviewed: this file provides a written proof and finite exact controls, not an independent mathematical review, a tensor target, or an exponent improvement.
+
+## Statement and coefficient convention
+
+Let K be any field, a >= 2, b >= 2, 1 <= e < b, and m = a+b-1. Consider
+
+    f(x,z) = c_0 + c_1*z + ... + c_(e-1)*z^(e-1) + w(x)*z^e,
+
+where c_s belongs to K, c_0 is nonzero, and w(x) is a nonzero polynomial of degree d < a. The coefficients below the highest z-power are constants; only the highest coefficient may depend on x.
+
+Define the literal cyclic-source coefficient matrix with rows (j,L), 0<=j<b and 0<=L<m; columns (H,r), 0<=H<m and 0<=r<a; and entry
+
+    R[(j,L),(H,r)] = coefficient of x^(H-j)*z^(L-r) in f.
+
+Out-of-range coefficients are zero. This is the full, untruncated source matrix used in the main-branch slice-rank discussion and PR #209.
+
+**Theorem.** Put q_j = floor((a+j)/e) for 0<=j<e. Then, over every field and every permitted choice of coefficients,
+
+    rank_K R_(a,b)(f) = a*b + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b, d*q_j).       (1)
+
+For d=0 the formula gives rank ab. Since sum_j q_j=a, when b>=d*ceil(a/e) the rank is exactly ab+ad. All statements hold without characteristic exceptions.
+
+For the genuinely three-term family f=1+z+(1+x^d)*z^2 with 1<=d<a and b>=3, (1) gives
+
+    rank = ab + min(b, d*floor(a/2)) + min(b, d*ceil(a/2)).
+
+For example, a=3,b=7,d=2 gives rank 27 and a=4,b=5,d=3 gives rank 30. These are neither binomial source slices nor diagonal polynomials f(xz). They do not construct compatible maps on three tensor legs.
+
+## Proof over an arbitrary field
+
+Only row groups L=0,...,a+e-1 can be nonzero, totaling (a+e)b active rows. Describe a linear dependence among those rows by polynomials
+
+    lambda_L(x) = sum_(j=0)^(b-1) lambda_(j,L)*x^j,
+    0<=L<=a+e-1,
+
+all of degree <b. Contracting against a column (H,r) reads the coefficient of x^H in
+
+    c_0*lambda_r + sum_(s=1)^(e-1) c_s*lambda_(r+s)
+                 + w(x)*lambda_(r+e).                           (2)
+
+Each expression in (2) has degree at most (a-1)+(b-1)=m-1. Because the literal matrix contains every H=0,...,m-1, the row dependence vanishes exactly when (2) vanishes as a complete polynomial identity for every r=0,...,a-1. In particular no highest-degree coefficient is dropped.
+
+The nonzero constant c_0 makes this a polynomial recurrence that can be solved backwards:
+
+    lambda_r = -(1/c_0)*(sum_(s=1)^(e-1) c_s*lambda_(r+s)
+                                + w*lambda_(r+e)),              (3)
+
+for r=a-1,...,0. Thus the e terminal polynomials lambda_a,...,lambda_(a+e-1) are freely chosen from K[x]. For j=0,...,e-1, define V_j by choosing terminal lambda_(a+j)=1 and all other terminal polynomials zero. These V_j form a free K[x]-basis of the complete polynomial solution module.
+
+Assume d>0. Each entry V_j(i) expands as a sum of paths from index i to terminal index a+j: a step of size s<e contributes the constant factor -c_s/c_0, while a step of size e contributes the polynomial factor -w/c_0. There can be at most q_j=floor((a+j)/e) size-e steps. Consequently every coordinate of V_j has degree at most delta_j=d*q_j.
+
+Write a+j=e*q_j+r_j with 0<=r_j<e. At coordinate i=r_j, the path with q_j size-e steps is the unique path attaining that number of polynomial steps: it consists entirely of size-e steps. Its leading coefficient is
+
+    (-lc(w)/c_0)^(q_j),                                    (4)
+
+which is nonzero. Every other path has fewer polynomial steps, so has degree strictly below delta_j. For every coordinate i>r_j, a path with q_j size-e steps would require a total step length at least e*q_j > a+j-i. Such a path cannot occur, so the degree-delta_j coefficient is zero. If q_j=0, the same statements hold because r_j=a+j is a free terminal coordinate, with V_j(r_j)=1 and V_j(i)=0 for all i>r_j.
+
+The residues r_j form a permutation of 0,...,e-1. Restrict the leading coefficient vector of each V_j at degree delta_j to the first e row-group coordinates. After ordering the columns by r_j, these vectors form a triangular e-by-e matrix with nonzero diagonal (4), because the entries with i>r_j vanish. Therefore the degree-delta_j leading coefficient vectors of all V_j are linearly independent over K, even in positive characteristic.
+
+For any polynomials P_j, not all zero, linear independence prevents cancellation at the largest weighted degree:
+
+    deg(sum_j P_j*V_j) = max_(j:P_j != 0)(deg(P_j)+delta_j),  (5)
+
+where degree of a polynomial vector means the maximum of its coordinate degrees. Thus all coordinates of the sum have degree <b if and only if each P_j separately satisfies deg(P_j)<b-delta_j. The active-row kernel therefore has dimension
+
+    sum_(j=0)^(e-1) max(0,b-d*q_j).                        (6)
+
+If d=0, all recurrence coefficients are constants and all V_j are constant vectors. Their terminal coordinates form the identity, so they remain independent and (5)-(6) hold with delta_j=0.
+
+Subtracting (6) from the (a+e)b active rows gives
+
+    (a+e)b - sum_j max(0,b-d*q_j)
+    = ab + sum_j min(b,d*q_j),
+
+proving (1). Write a=e*k+r, 0<=r<e. Exactly r of the q_j equal k+1 and the rest equal k; hence sum_j q_j=e*k+r=a. This proves the corollary. QED.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent literal-source finite-field check of the top-coefficient biform rank theorem.
+
+Uses only the Python standard library. The rank oracle builds the complete
+coefficient matrix, including its zero rows, rather than using the syzygy proof.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def coefficient_matrix(a: int, b: int, e: int, c: tuple[int, ...], w: tuple[int, ...], p: int):
+    """The literal R_(a,b) rows (j,L), columns (H,r)."""
+    assert a >= 2 and b > e >= 1 and len(c) == e and len(w) == a
+    m = a + b - 1
+    M = [[0] * (a * m) for _ in range(b * m)]
+    # Build from source coefficients directly, never from the recurrence.
+    for r in range(a):
+        for j in range(b):
+            for s, coefficient in enumerate(c):
+                row = j * m + (r + s)
+                col = j * a + r  # column index is actually H*a+r; H=j.
+                M[row][col] = (M[row][col] + coefficient) % p
+            for k, coefficient in enumerate(w):
+                if coefficient:
+                    row = j * m + (r + e)
+                    col = (j + k) * a + r
+                    M[row][col] = (M[row][col] + coefficient) % p
+    return M
+
+
+def exact_rank_modp(M: list[list[int]], p: int) -> int:
+    A = [row[:] for row in M]
+    nrows = len(A)
+    ncols = len(A[0])
+    rank = 0
+    for col in range(ncols):
+        pivot = next((i for i in range(rank, nrows) if A[i][col] % p), None)
+        if pivot is None:
+            continue
+        A[rank], A[pivot] = A[pivot], A[rank]
+        inv = pow(A[rank][col] % p, -1, p)
+        A[rank][col:] = [(x * inv) % p for x in A[rank][col:]]
+        for i in range(rank + 1, nrows):
+            multiplier = A[i][col] % p
+            if multiplier:
+                A[i][col:] = [(x - multiplier * y) % p for x, y in zip(A[i][col:], A[rank][col:])]
+        rank += 1
+        if rank == nrows:
+            break
+    return rank
+
+
+def predicted_rank(a: int, b: int, e: int, w: tuple[int, ...], p: int) -> int:
+    deg = max(k for k, coeff in enumerate(w) if coeff % p)
+    return a * b + sum(min(b, deg * ((a + j) // e)) for j in range(e))
+
+

+    expected = predicted_rank(a, b, e, w, p)
+    got = exact_rank_modp(coefficient_matrix(a, b, e, c, w, p), p)

+        raise AssertionError(f"R({a},{b}) e={e}, c={c}, w={w} over F_{p}: expected {expected}, got {got}")

+

+    x ^= (x << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    x ^= x >> 17
+    x ^= (x << 5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    return x & 0xFFFFFFFF
+

+    # Fixed-seed, broad rectangular spectrum; coefficients are unrestricted.
+    rng = 0xB1F0A26E
+    for p in (5, 7, 101):
+        for a in range(2, 8):
+            for e in range(2, 6):

+                    c = []
+                    for i in range(e):

+                        c.append((rng % (p - 1)) + 1 if i == 0 else rng % p)

pull.body:
## Why

Parallel research branches contain overlapping packages, claim records, and validation receipts. This PR combines the recorded work into one reviewable tree and preserves the exact source versions needed to retire superseded PRs and branches.

## Changes

- Consolidate **132 topic branch names and 159 archived source snapshots**, with exact heads, source PR metadata, and recovery tags in the [branch manifest](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/matrix-mult-bounds/blob/consolidation/all-branches-20261023/docs/consolidation/2026-10-23/branches.json).
- Preserve **607 claim records** and their evidence statuses. Disambiguate independent records and package implementations, retain their tests and certificates, and reconcile shared summaries without losing later scope corrections or attribution.
- Preserve both historical research archives byte-for-byte. Record source selection, restored paths, and conflict decisions in the [consolidation guide](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/matrix-mult-bounds/blob/consolidation/all-branches-20261023/docs/consolidation/2026-10-23/PUBLICATION.md) and [resolution manifest](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/matrix-mult-bounds/blob/consolidation/all-branches-20261023/docs/consolidation/2026-10-23/central_resolution_manifest.json).
- Correct `AI-OBLIQUE-PAIRED-REPAIR-001` in `5d144109`: the first residual rank is **at least** `r^2-b^2` for every first map, and the supplied first map attains equality. The [correction addendum](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/matrix-mult-bounds/blob/5d1441090e1c3c804d0ba0797a20ec303b5c08d5/docs/consolidation/2026-10-23/claim_resolution.json) retains the original source record and explains the three dependent metadata updates.
- Keep the full four-group Python 3.10/3.14 test matrix, five historical archive replays, and auxiliary scalar-profile Lean build behind required `CI`. The selective-test proposal remains inactive.

## Validation

| Local stage | Result |
|---|---|
| Full baseline, `caf51fe` | 1,916 tests executed: 1,914 passed and two dependency-pin checks failed. Both stale requirements hashes were repaired with original metadata retained. |
| Focused follow-up, `e2baf117` | All 29 checks passed, including the repaired pins and affected packages. |
| Eight-head catch-up, `8a53354c` | All 33 checks and the standalone quadratic equal-degree verifier passed. |
| Final closure tree, `9354de63` | Both metadata/pin checks passed; active code, test files, witnesses, claims, and dependencies remain identical to the preceding passing tree. |
| Historical replay | All five archived experiments passed. |
| Scoped claim correction, tree `92bce7a7` (published as `5d144109`) | All 13 focused checks passed: eight repository checks, three archive-integrity checks, and two oblique-repair identity/boundary checks. An isolated zero-first-map control confirms why the universal claim must state a lower bound. |

The [validation receipts](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/matrix-mult-bounds/tree/consolidation/all-branches-20261023/docs/consolidation/2026-10-23/validation) identify each tested revision and its coverage. The final inventory contains **1,933 tests**. Its passing coverage combines the baseline and focused follow-ups; the full final tree has not had one uninterrupted local regression run.

The correction's targeted preservation checks verified all 607 current claim hashes, 1,317 resolution-output hashes, and 79 packaged-evidence hashes. The other 606 claim records, original source hashes, proof/code/witness files, archives, and historical receipts remain unchanged. This verifies the narrow correction against its parent; it is not a new full preservation audit or full regression run, and the 13 rechecks do not increase the test inventory.

**Final-head hosted CI remains required**, including the complete Python matrix, archive replay, and Lean build. Merge also requires the current-main base and resolved review discussions. Main remains unchanged until these PR gates pass.

## Research and retirement scope

Consolidation does not establish an improved exponent or independent mathematical review. Written proofs, conditional implications, and finite experiments retain their recorded status. The Lean project formalizes the auxiliary finite slope lemma, not the complete scalar-profile proof.

Source PRs are closed **as superseded by this PR**, rather than recorded as individually merged. Original bodies and draft metadata remain preserved. A source branch is deleted only when its current head exactly matches an archived, incorporated commit, has no remaining open PR dependency, and is neither protected nor a default/integration branch. Atomic deletion leases retain concurrently advanced heads. At 17:56 UTC, cleanup has verified **127 source branches deleted** and **100 source PRs closed as superseded**. All deleted heads retain exact recovery tags. The remaining five topic branches contain newly captured work being integrated in a separately validated follow-up; they are not part of this 159-snapshot revision.
